neighbours.label: tokens in advice on handling a poisoning or swallowed-substance emergency (it should be taken to a vet, empty the stomach)
fire: If your puppy has swallowed rat poison, it must be brought to an emergency clinic.
When a toddler swallows pills, the first step is to call poison control.
If the cat licked antifreeze, it needs treatment within hours.
The vet may induce vomiting to empty the dog's stomach.
If you accidentally take two tablets, it is usually not dangerous, but call your pharmacist.
Should your rabbit chew a toxic plant, it should be seen by a vet the same day.
Doctors flushed the boy's stomach after he drank the cleaning fluid.
If a horse eats yew leaves, it can die within hours.
quiet: If your puppy has chewed the sofa, it must be trained more firmly.
When a toddler spills juice, the first step is to fetch a towel.
If the cat scratched the door, it needs a new scratching post.
The groomer may trim the dog's nails during the bath.
If you accidentally buy two tickets, it is usually easy to get a refund.
Should your rabbit escape the hutch, it should be found before dark.
Parents cleaned the boy's shoes after he walked through mud.
If a horse loses a shoe, it can still be ridden gently.

notes: Probe: poisoned-pet 'it should be' 0.39-0.46, 'stomach' 0.38, missed-dose 'it' 0.20, car 'it' 0.06. The + pole is lost/found/orphan return.
